What’s up Voat?!? My name is Mark and I am a forum lurker. I suppose my early memories of watching conversations unfold online took place during the IRC days. A/S/L anyone? IGN’s Vestibule was also a frequently visited site of my youth. Slashdot was good for a while.

As I grew older, Reddit was my go-to place on the web. I’ve seen that site grow and evolve and devolve over the years. As most of you know, the early days were mostly tech and science content, but as the user base grew, the posts became more and more juvenile. I personally think the Digg crash helped accelerate the processes, but at the end of the day the highest voted link or comment made it to the top. It was a true democracy in that way.

And that was the double edged sword of the site. I didn’t really like the advice animal memes that seemed to dominate the site a few years back, but it was what the user base wanted. I sometimes agreed and sometimes disagreed with users in the comment sections. I didn’t melt when someone wrote something that I didn’t like. Who am I to argue if that is what the community collectively wants?

Then the changes started happening... slowly at first. Tweaking the default subs proved to be a great way to control the narrative. Heavy handed moderation started becoming more prevalent, AMAs became more controlled, and shadowbans transitioned from a last ditch solution to minimize spammers to a regular tool to silence “unpopular” speech.

Of course “unpopular” implies that the majority disagrees with the statement. It is sort of hard to call a statement “unpopular” when it is the highest ranked comment, but that is another issue; everyone knows what I’m talking about here. As an aside, I will say that the final straw for me was seeing a post in r/news with 4,000 comments get completely and totally nuked. You mean to tell me that every single comment out of 4,000 violated the arbitrary rules you’ve made up? I’ve digressed. Let me refocus.

What concerns me more than the destruction of Reddit is the widespread censorship of speech across the internet. CNN, Fox News and Huffington all regularly disable discussions on topics deemed too toxic for the people to discuss. Oh sure, they’ll let you talk about the new iPhone or whatever celebrity nonsense is in the news that day. But once feelings get hurt, they have to shut it down. CNN (and it pains me to say this) is probably the most consistent in that they don’t allow conversations for most topics anymore. That actually doesn’t really bother me so much just because they (mostly) apply it universally.

And unfortunately the new media ventures are just as bad – if not worse – than their traditional media counterparts. Both Vox and Gawker are so unapologetically biased I cannot even be bothered to visit their sites anymore. Vox in particular is very heavy handed with their comment moderation to the point of banning anyone who disagrees with whatever bogus claim their writers make. Facts and reality don’t matter really.

I’ll give you a non-controversial example.

During the height of the net neutrality debate, The Verge (Vox) wrote some pretty one-sided articles on the issue. Now to be fair, I agree generally with the stance they take on net neutrality, however, it is hard for me to see them as an unbiased source when they title articles like this…

"Why you should be scared of Comcast and Time Warner Cable Merging"

"The anti-net neutrality coalition is a sham"

"The internet is fucked (but we can fix it)"

"Thank you, America, for finally acting sane about the internet"

And when someone points out their bias in the comment section, they get banned. I’ve seen it happen several times. That’s what we lurkers do - lurk and observe.

(Deep breath)

That’s all great and dandy. If a site wants to live in an echo chamber, fine by me. It’s a free world and for the most part these people are limited to said echo chambers. They are businesses and we as consumers can take our page views and ad revenue somewhere else. Adblock is not enough. Ghostery is not enough. You have to totally and completely stop visiting sites that censor. It’s hard I know.

What really concerns me most is the speed at which these power hungry people took over the site which shall not be named. I see some of these “my way is the only way” types seeping into real world and that keeps me up at night.

“You can’t say that.”

“You can’t draw that.”

“You can’t think that.”

Hold on to your hats boy and girls! Freedom of speech is not safe. As an American, I’d like to think that our first amendment is secure, but I’m not so sure many people agree with the idea of free speech anymore. It seems often people say, “I believe in free speech, but…”

In closing I want to leave you with one of my favorite quotes. I first heard it on a Boards of Canada track, but apparently it is originally from a film titled “A Brief Affair.” I don’t really think I understood when I first heard it, but maybe these trends are circular.

"If you can be told what you can see or read, then it follows that you can be told what to say or think. Defend your constitutionally protected rights - no one else will do it for you. Thank you.”
